scope: New synthetic transfer examples authored after inspection of development results. Separate from first benchmark; not a blinded or independently adjudicated holdout. Do not tune on these cases and then report them as independent validation.

cases.anchor: My hands adjusted the oar whenever the current pulled the boat sideways, before I could explain what I was doing.

candidates.text: Practitioners may express tacit knowledge through adjustments to a changing situation.
Oars are available in wood, aluminum and carbon fiber.
Ocean currents transport heat between regions.

cases.reason: Embodied practical knowledge; no claim about conscious intention of water.

cases.anchor: We called the vacant strip an eyesore until I saw the butterflies feeding there.

candidates.text: Labels can shape which ecological values a community recognizes or overlooks.
Vacant properties can be surveyed using satellite imagery.
Butterflies are insects with four wings.

cases.anchor: My brother prepared my mother's meals every morning, and nobody mentioned those hours when we discussed the household's finances.

candidates.text: Unpaid maintenance and caregiving often sustain households without appearing in economic accounts.
Breakfast can provide nutrients before work.
Households may compare interest rates when borrowing.

cases.reason: Recognition of care work without assuming exploitation.

cases.anchor: Our landlord said that we could not plant food in the yard, even though we would pay for the seeds ourselves.

candidates.text: Control over access to land can limit people's practical choices and independence.
Seeds can be started indoors before the last frost.
Yards can be measured for landscaping.

cases.anchor: The scraps from our meals go into the soil that supports the vegetables we eat.

candidates.text: Nutrient cycling connects decomposition to renewed biological production.
A gift economy emphasizes responding to what sustains us.
Household waste containers come in different sizes.

cases.reason: Two routes, ecological process and ethical reciprocity; the latter is an interpretive question, not proven intention.

cases.anchor: Because I grew up in the town, the film's account of its factory seemed familiar; my classmate noticed a history I had never heard.

candidates.text: An observer's social position and prior experiences influence interpretation and blind spots.
A film can be projected at different resolutions.
Manufacturing output is often reported quarterly.

cases.anchor: The assignment file is named draft two and is due at midnight.

candidates.text: A novelist revised her childhood memories.
Darkness changes insect navigation.
Teachers may negotiate institutional expectations.

cases.reason: Routine logistical entry; shared terms alone do not establish a meaningful connection.

cases.anchor: My uncle allowed me to listen to his account but explicitly asked me not to quote it.

candidates.text: Research consent should include the specific uses of interview material.
Direct quotations may preserve a speaker's wording.
Relatives often know family history.

cases.reason: Respect explicit restriction; no automatic invitation.

cases.anchor: I have enough evidence for this section. I am going to compare the two readings before I write the next one.

candidates.text: A synthesis may compare theoretical frameworks rather than simply summarize authors.
A reading journal may contain page locators.

cases.reason: The student already states a next step.

cases.anchor: I am recording the position and sound of the insects before interpreting the scene.

candidates.text: Field observations can be separated from interpretation.
Insects may communicate through sound.

cases.anchor: The interviewee said, “I don't need another question.” I wondered whether her choice to stop might reveal a limit of my authority as an interviewer.

candidates.text: Interviewers should recognize unequal power and allow participants to shape the encounter.
Questionnaires can be divided into sections.
Quotation marks identify a speaker's words.

cases.reason: The student reflects on authority; quoted self-direction is not the student's own instruction.

cases.anchor: I distinguish the response I observed from my interpretation of the animal's intentions. I am comfortable leaving the latter uncertain.

candidates.text: Observable behavior cannot by itself establish conscious purpose.
Animal movements can be measured in a laboratory.

cases.reason: Already developed distinction and explicit uncertainty; no pressure.
